notes: oracle tiers (item fathomcue, calibration/oracles/fathom-cue): sym_* (L1) and ref_* (L2) are tier A. The oracle is the cue binary v0.16.1 as separate processes, never fathom's loader: `cue export --out json` names what exists (including what a comprehension generates, which only evaluation names), `cue lsp` documentSymbol gives each range and textDocument/definition each reference (calibration/oracles/cue). A written entity's range is the language server's field; a generated one's is the dynamic field it lists. Structure is graded beside the metrics, tier A and not one of them: cue vet -d against schema/project, schema/semantic and schema/rules/archconformance passes on all fixtures. The repository's own file has 41 concerns (14 written, 27 generated) and one reference (the concerns block to its hidden _intentDocs table); the second subject is the in-repo fixture calibration/oracles/fathom-cue/fixtures/concerns (their subject sha is the fathom commit measured at, not a pinned external repository), which carries 3 written and 2 generated concerns and 5 references the repository's file does not: L2 rests mostly on it. The subjects are tiny too (46 entities, two files): the throughput gate reads 1.2 to 3 MB/s run to run because the evaluator's per-file cost dominates a 12 KB file, and the committed reading is a run that met it (the cue dialect's extraction is the same code)

scope: the dialect composes the CUE extraction (references are the CUE extraction's own) and adds a concern entity per `concerns:` member. Not read: concern-to-rule citations (the next gap), the shipped packs `packs:` names, and the files a check names (cross-file, L3)
per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)
